gaps.title: Compliance Gap: Itemised Notice in Plain Language & 8th Schedule Availability
gaps.condition_identified: Missing documented operational process for Itemised Notice in Plain Language & 8th Schedule Availability.
gaps.why_it_matters: Section Section 5 mandates verifiable controls. Non-compliance exposes the organisation to penalties under the DPDP Act.
gaps.recommended_solution: Draft a clear, itemised notice detailing specific data points (e.g., patient phone, medical report), exact operational purpose (e.g., diagnostic consultation), rights procedure, and contact details of the Grievance Officer.

gaps.title: Compliance Gap: Data Fiduciary Responsibility & Processor Oversight
gaps.condition_identified: Missing documented operational process for Data Fiduciary Responsibility & Processor Oversight.
gaps.why_it_matters: Section Section 8(1) & 8(2) mandates verifiable controls. Non-compliance exposes the organisation to penalties under the DPDP Act.
gaps.recommended_solution: Execute DPDP-compliant DPAs with all third-party software, cloud storage providers, and billing vendors binding them to process data solely on instruction and implement safeguards.

gaps.title: Compliance Gap: Personal Data Breach Intimation
gaps.condition_identified: Missing documented operational process for Personal Data Breach Intimation.
gaps.why_it_matters: Section Section 8(6) mandates verifiable controls. Non-compliance exposes the organisation to penalties under the DPDP Act.
gaps.recommended_solution: Establish a dual-stage breach response workflow: (1) Immediate preliminary intimation to Data Protection Board upon confirmation, (2) Detailed forensic intimation within 72 hours, with direct communication to affected Data Principals.

remediation_tasks.description:
Under Section 5, every Data Fiduciary must give Data Principals an itemised notice before or at the time of requesting personal data, stating the personal data categories, processing purpose, manner of exercising rights, and grievance details.

Recommended: Draft and publish a clear, standalone, business-specific Privacy Notice compliant with Section 5 and Rule 3 itemised notice standards.

org-clinic-test-1.title: Arogya Diagnostics Clinic Customer & Patient Privacy Notice
org-clinic-test-1.content:
ITEMISED PRIVACY NOTICE
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Section 5 read with Rule 3)

1. Identity of Data Fiduciary:
Arogya Diagnostics Clinic (Address: Registered Office, India)

2. Personal Data Collected & Processing Purposes:
We collect and process digital personal data solely for specified lawful purposes:
• Patient Demographic Information: Patient identification, contact, appointment scheduling (Basis: DPDP Section 6 (Consent) & Section 5 Notice)
• Medical & Clinical Diagnostic Reports: Medical diagnosis, pathology analysis, treatment planning (Basis: DPDP Section 6 (Consent) & Section 7(e) Medical Emergency)
• Billing, Invoice & Insurance Records: Invoice generation, payment reconciliation, insurance TPA claims (Basis: DPDP Section 7(c) (Legal Obligation) & Section 6)
• Employee & Medical Staff Records: Employment administration, salary processing, medical credentialing (Basis: DPDP Section 7(i) (Employment purposes))

3. Your Statutory Rights as Data Principal (Sections 11–14):
You possess statutory rights to:
• Right to Access: Obtain a summary of your personal data and third parties shared with.
• Right to Correction & Updating: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete records.
• Right to Erasure: Request erasure where statutory clinical or legal retention does not mandate preservation.
• Right to Withdraw Consent: Withdraw consent at any time with the same ease as provided (Section 6(4)).
• Right to Nominate: Nominate a representative in the event of death or incapacity (Section 14).

4. Grievance Redressal Mechanism (Section 8(10) & Rule 9):
If you have any questions, rights requests, or grievances regarding your personal data:
Grievance Officer: Data Protection Grievance Officer
Email: grievance@organisation.com
Address: Registered Office, India
We endeavor to investigate and redress all grievances within thirty (30) business days.

5. Multilingual Availability:
This notice is prepared in English and is available in Hindi and other Eighth Schedule languages upon request at our reception desk or customer support portal.

findings.title: Privacy Notice Not Detected on Public Pages
findings.observation: No accessible Privacy Policy or Data Protection Notice was found among 3 scanned public pages.
findings.evidence_snippet: Searched standard footer anchors, sitemaps, and common paths (/privacy, /privacy-policy, /data-protection). None returned valid notice content.
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 5, every Data Fiduciary must give Data Principals an itemised notice before or at the time of requesting personal data, stating the personal data categories, processing purpose, manner of exercising rights, and grievance details.
findings.recommended_action: Draft and publish a clear, standalone, business-specific Privacy Notice compliant with Section 5 and Rule 3 itemised notice standards.
findings.required_evidence: Published Privacy Notice URL and internal Board / Management approval sign-off.
findings.statutory_disclaimer: These are statutory maximum penalty ceilings enumerated under the Schedule to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not predicted, automated, or actual fines. Actual penalties are determined solely by the Data Protection Board of India on a case-by-case basis under Section 28 and Section 33, evaluating nature, gravity, duration, repetitive nature, and mitigating actions taken. Most substantive obligations are scheduled to take effect on 13 May 2027.

findings.title: Pre-Selected Consent Checkbox Detected on Public Form
findings.observation: A consent or agreement checkbox in form 'quick-book' was observed in a pre-checked state by default.
findings.evidence_snippet: HTML element <input type='checkbox' checked> detected with consent wording: 'I agree to communications'
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 6(1), consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and an unambiguous indication through clear affirmative action. Pre-ticked boxes are deemed invalid consent under Indian DPDP regulatory interpretations.
findings.recommended_action: Ensure all consent checkboxes default to un-ticked, requiring an active affirmative gesture by the Data Principal.
findings.required_evidence: Updated form markup confirming default unselected state.
findings.statutory_disclaimer: These are statutory maximum penalty ceilings enumerated under the Schedule to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not predicted, automated, or actual fines. Actual penalties are determined solely by the Data Protection Board of India on a case-by-case basis under Section 28 and Section 33, evaluating nature, gravity, duration, repetitive nature, and mitigating actions taken. Most substantive obligations are scheduled to take effect on 13 May 2027.

findings.title: Data Collection Form Lacks Nearby Privacy Notice Reference
findings.observation: Public form collects Full Name / Identity, Phone / Mobile Number without an accompanying privacy notice link or purpose explanation adjacent to the submit action.
findings.evidence_snippet: Form at https://medicare.example.in has inputs: ['patient_name', 'phone', 'agree'] but no nearby privacy notice reference.
findings.why_it_matters: Data Principals should be informed of the purpose and privacy terms at or before the moment personal data is collected.
findings.recommended_action: Add a clear statement adjacent to the form submit button: 'We process your details in accordance with our Privacy Notice [Link] for appointment and consultation purposes.'
findings.required_evidence: Screenshot of updated form with adjacent notice hyperlink.

findings.title: Published Grievance Redressal Contact Not Detected
findings.observation: No Grievance Redressal Officer or dedicated privacy contact information was discovered on the public website.
findings.evidence_snippet: Searched scanned pages for 'Grievance Officer', 'Data Protection Officer', or dedicated privacy contact details.
findings.why_it_matters: Section 8(9) requires every Data Fiduciary to establish an effective grievance redressal mechanism and publish the contact details of the Grievance Officer on its website so Data Principals can seek redressal prior to approaching the Board.
findings.recommended_action: Publish the name, designation, and official email address of your Grievance Redressal Officer on your contact and privacy pages.
findings.required_evidence: Published Grievance Officer section and appointment record.

findings.title: Observable Third-Party Trackers & Services Detected (3 Services)
findings.observation: Public website loads external services: Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel (Facebook), Razorpay Payment Gateway.
findings.evidence_snippet: Observed script requests: ['https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-DEMO123', 'https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js', 'https://checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js']
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 8(2), a Data Fiduciary may only engage a Data Processor under a valid contract that ensures compliance with the Act. Furthermore, third-party sharing must be itemised in privacy notices under Section 5.
findings.recommended_action: 1. Verify whether Data Processor Agreements (DPAs) with standard DPDP safeguards are executed with each provider. 2. Log them in your internal Vendor Register. 3. Update the privacy notice to disclose these processing partners.
findings.required_evidence: Executed Data Processor Agreements and entry in internal Vendor Register.

findings.title: Verifiable Parental Consent Mechanism Not Observed for Children's Data
findings.legal_reference: Section 9(1) & October 2026 Removal of Difficulties Order
findings.observation: Website context indicates services for minors / students / pediatric patients, but no verifiable parental or guardian consent workflow was observed.
findings.evidence_snippet: Selected industry: 'healthcare'; no parental consent disclosures detected on public intake forms.
findings.why_it_matters: Section 9(1) strictly mandates that a Data Fiduciary must obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian before processing any personal data of a child. Section 9(2) and (3) strictly prohibit tracking, behavioral monitoring, or targeted ads directed at children.
findings.recommended_action: Implement a verifiable parental/guardian consent verification step during child registration, and ensure analytics scripts are disabled for minor user journeys.
findings.required_evidence: Documented parental consent workflow and guardian verification log.
findings.statutory_disclaimer: These are statutory maximum penalty ceilings enumerated under the Schedule to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not predicted, automated, or actual fines. Actual penalties are determined solely by the Data Protection Board of India on a case-by-case basis under Section 28 and Section 33, evaluating nature, gravity, duration, repetitive nature, and mitigating actions taken. Most substantive obligations are scheduled to take effect on 13 May 2027.

findings.title: Perimeter HTTP Security Headers Missing (3 Headers)
findings.observation: Public web server does not return: HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security), Clickjacking Protection (X-Frame-Options), MIME-Sniffing Defense (X-Content-Type-Options).
findings.evidence_snippet: Observed headers: ['server', 'content-type']
findings.why_it_matters: HTTP security headers provide essential baseline perimeter hardening against clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and insecure downgrade attacks on personal data.
findings.recommended_action: Configure your reverse proxy, CDN, or web server to append HSTS, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff headers.
findings.required_evidence: Server header configuration file.
findings.statutory_disclaimer: These are statutory maximum penalty ceilings enumerated under the Schedule to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not predicted, automated, or actual fines. Actual penalties are determined solely by the Data Protection Board of India on a case-by-case basis under Section 28 and Section 33, evaluating nature, gravity, duration, repetitive nature, and mitigating actions taken. Most substantive obligations are scheduled to take effect on 13 May 2027.

findings.title: Internal Controls & Backend Systems Require DPDP Assessment
findings.observation: Public website scanning cannot inspect internal database encryption at rest, employee role-based access, backup restoration drills, or purpose-based retention schedules.
findings.evidence_snippet: Inherent limitation of external perimeter inspection.
findings.why_it_matters: Full statutory DPDP compliance requires internal governance, employee training, data retention schedules, and breach notification readiness that cannot be verified from outside.
findings.recommended_action: Continue with the TrustAudit Full Internal DPDP Assessment to evaluate your RoPA inventory, retention schedules, and evidence vault.
findings.required_evidence: Completed DPDP Internal Assessment questionnaire.

findings.title: Pre-Selected Consent Checkbox Detected on Public Form
findings.observation: A consent or agreement checkbox in form 'quick-book' was observed in a pre-checked state by default.
findings.evidence_snippet: HTML element <input type='checkbox' checked> detected with consent wording: 'I agree to communications'

findings.title: Pre-Selected Consent Checkbox Detected on Public Form
findings.observation: A consent or agreement checkbox in form 'quick-book' was observed in a pre-checked state by default.
findings.evidence_snippet: HTML element <input type='checkbox' checked> detected with consent wording: 'I agree to communications'

findings.required_evidence: Updated form markup confirming default unselected state.

findings.title: Pre-Selected Consent Checkbox Detected on Public Form
findings.observation: A consent or agreement checkbox in form 'quick-book' was observed in a pre-checked state by default.
findings.evidence_snippet: HTML element <input type='checkbox' checked> detected with consent wording: 'I agree to communications'
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 6(1), consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and an unambiguous indication through clear affirmative action. Pre-ticked boxes are deemed invalid consent under Indian DPDP regulatory interpretations.
findings.recommended_action: Ensure all consent checkboxes default to un-ticked, requiring an active affirmative gesture by the Data Principal.
findings.required_evidence: Updated form markup confirming default unselected state.

findings.title: Pre-Selected Consent Checkbox Detected on Public Form
findings.observation: A consent or agreement checkbox in form 'quick-book' was observed in a pre-checked state by default.
findings.evidence_snippet: HTML element <input type='checkbox' checked> detected with consent wording: 'I agree to communications'
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 6(1), consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and an unambiguous indication through clear affirmative action. Pre-ticked boxes are deemed invalid consent under Indian DPDP regulatory interpretations.
findings.recommended_action: Ensure all consent checkboxes default to un-ticked, requiring an active affirmative gesture by the Data Principal.
findings.required_evidence: Updated form markup confirming default unselected state.

findings.title: Privacy Notice Not Detected on Public Pages
findings.observation: No accessible Privacy Policy or Data Protection Notice was found among 3 scanned public pages.
findings.evidence_snippet: Searched standard footer anchors, sitemaps, and common paths (/privacy, /privacy-policy, /data-protection). None returned valid notice content.
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 5, every Data Fiduciary must give Data Principals an itemised notice before or at the time of requesting personal data, stating the personal data categories, processing purpose, manner of exercising rights, and grievance details.

findings.required_evidence: Published Privacy Notice URL and internal Board / Management approval sign-off.

findings.title: Pre-Selected Consent Checkbox Detected on Public Form
findings.observation: A consent or agreement checkbox in form 'quick-book' was observed in a pre-checked state by default.
findings.evidence_snippet: HTML element <input type='checkbox' checked> detected with consent wording: 'I agree to communications'
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 6(1), consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and an unambiguous indication through clear affirmative action. Pre-ticked boxes are deemed invalid consent under Indian DPDP regulatory interpretations.
findings.recommended_action: Ensure all consent checkboxes default to un-ticked, requiring an active affirmative gesture by the Data Principal.
findings.required_evidence: Updated form markup confirming default unselected state.

findings.observation: Public website loads external services: Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel (Facebook), Razorpay Payment Gateway.

findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 8(2), a Data Fiduciary may only engage a Data Processor under a valid contract that ensures compliance with the Act. Furthermore, third-party sharing must be itemised in privacy notices under Section 5.

findings.title: Verifiable Parental Consent Mechanism Not Observed for Children's Data
findings.legal_reference: Section 9(1) & October 2026 Removal of Difficulties Order
findings.observation: Website context indicates services for minors / students / pediatric patients, but no verifiable parental or guardian consent workflow was observed.
findings.evidence_snippet: Selected industry: 'healthcare'; no parental consent disclosures detected on public intake forms.
findings.why_it_matters: Section 9(1) strictly mandates that a Data Fiduciary must obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian before processing any personal data of a child. Section 9(2) and (3) strictly prohibit tracking, behavioral monitoring, or targeted ads directed at children.
findings.recommended_action: Implement a verifiable parental/guardian consent verification step during child registration, and ensure analytics scripts are disabled for minor user journeys.
findings.required_evidence: Documented parental consent workflow and guardian verification log.

findings.title: Perimeter HTTP Security Headers Missing (3 Headers)
findings.observation: Public web server does not return: HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security), Clickjacking Protection (X-Frame-Options), MIME-Sniffing Defense (X-Content-Type-Options).
findings.evidence_snippet: Observed headers: ['server', 'content-type']
findings.why_it_matters: HTTP security headers provide essential baseline perimeter hardening against clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and insecure downgrade attacks on personal data.
findings.recommended_action: Configure your reverse proxy, CDN, or web server to append HSTS, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff headers.
findings.required_evidence: Server header configuration file.

findings.title: Privacy Notice Not Detected on Public Pages
findings.observation: No accessible Privacy Policy or Data Protection Notice was found among 3 scanned public pages.
findings.evidence_snippet: Searched standard footer anchors, sitemaps, and common paths (/privacy, /privacy-policy, /data-protection). None returned valid notice content.
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 5, every Data Fiduciary must give Data Principals an itemised notice before or at the time of requesting personal data, stating the personal data categories, processing purpose, manner of exercising rights, and grievance details.
findings.recommended_action: Draft and publish a clear, standalone, business-specific Privacy Notice compliant with Section 5 and Rule 3 itemised notice standards.
findings.required_evidence: Published Privacy Notice URL and internal Board / Management approval sign-off.

Most substantive obligations are scheduled to take effect on 13 May 2027.

findings.title: Pre-Selected Consent Checkbox Detected on Public Form
findings.observation: A consent or agreement checkbox in form 'quick-book' was observed in a pre-checked state by default.
findings.evidence_snippet: HTML element <input type='checkbox' checked> detected with consent wording: 'I agree to communications'
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 6(1), consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and an unambiguous indication through clear affirmative action. Pre-ticked boxes are deemed invalid consent under Indian DPDP regulatory interpretations.
findings.recommended_action: Ensure all consent checkboxes default to un-ticked, requiring an active affirmative gesture by the Data Principal.
findings.required_evidence: Updated form markup confirming default unselected state.

findings.title: Data Collection Form Lacks Nearby Privacy Notice Reference
findings.observation: Public form collects Full Name / Identity, Phone / Mobile Number without an accompanying privacy notice link or purpose explanation adjacent to the submit action.
findings.evidence_snippet: Form at https://clinicb.in has inputs: ['patient_name', 'phone', 'agree'] but no nearby privacy notice reference.
findings.why_it_matters: Data Principals should be informed of the purpose and privacy terms at or before the moment personal data is collected.
findings.recommended_action: Add a clear statement adjacent to the form submit button: 'We process your details in accordance with our Privacy Notice [Link] for appointment and consultation purposes.'

findings.observation: No Grievance Redressal Officer or dedicated privacy contact information was discovered on the public website.

findings.title: Observable Third-Party Trackers & Services Detected (3 Services)
findings.observation: Public website loads external services: Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel (Facebook), Razorpay Payment Gateway.
findings.evidence_snippet: Observed script requests: ['https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-DEMO123', 'https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js', 'https://checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js']
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 8(2), a Data Fiduciary may only engage a Data Processor under a valid contract that ensures compliance with the Act. Furthermore, third-party sharing must be itemised in privacy notices under Section 5.
findings.recommended_action: 1. Verify whether Data Processor Agreements (DPAs) with standard DPDP safeguards are executed with each provider. 2. Log them in your internal Vendor Register. 3. Update the privacy notice to disclose these processing partners.
findings.required_evidence: Executed Data Processor Agreements and entry in internal Vendor Register.

findings.title: Verifiable Parental Consent Mechanism Not Observed for Children's Data
findings.legal_reference: Section 9(1) & October 2026 Removal of Difficulties Order
findings.observation: Website context indicates services for minors / students / pediatric patients, but no verifiable parental or guardian consent workflow was observed.
findings.evidence_snippet: Selected industry: 'healthcare'; no parental consent disclosures detected on public intake forms.
findings.why_it_matters: Section 9(1) strictly mandates that a Data Fiduciary must obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian before processing any personal data of a child. Section 9(2) and (3) strictly prohibit tracking, behavioral monitoring, or targeted ads directed at children.
findings.recommended_action: Implement a verifiable parental/guardian consent verification step during child registration, and ensure analytics scripts are disabled for minor user journeys.
findings.required_evidence: Documented parental consent workflow and guardian verification log.

findings.title: Perimeter HTTP Security Headers Missing (3 Headers)
findings.observation: Public web server does not return: HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security), Clickjacking Protection (X-Frame-Options), MIME-Sniffing Defense (X-Content-Type-Options).
findings.evidence_snippet: Observed headers: ['server', 'content-type']
findings.why_it_matters: HTTP security headers provide essential baseline perimeter hardening against clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and insecure downgrade attacks on personal data.
findings.recommended_action: Configure your reverse proxy, CDN, or web server to append HSTS, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff headers.
findings.required_evidence: Server header configuration file.
findings.statutory_disclaimer: These are statutory maximum penalty ceilings enumerated under the Schedule to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, not predicted, automated, or actual fines. Most substantive obligations are scheduled to take effect on 13 May 2027.

findings.title: Internal Controls & Backend Systems Require DPDP Assessment
findings.observation: Public website scanning cannot inspect internal database encryption at rest, employee role-based access, backup restoration drills, or purpose-based retention schedules.
findings.evidence_snippet: Inherent limitation of external perimeter inspection.
findings.why_it_matters: Full statutory DPDP compliance requires internal governance, employee training, data retention schedules, and breach notification readiness that cannot be verified from outside.
findings.recommended_action: Continue with the TrustAudit Full Internal DPDP Assessment to evaluate your RoPA inventory, retention schedules, and evidence vault.
findings.required_evidence: Completed DPDP Internal Assessment questionnaire.

findings.title: Pre-Selected Consent Checkbox Detected on Public Form
findings.observation: A consent or agreement checkbox in form 'quick-book' was observed in a pre-checked state by default.
findings.evidence_snippet: HTML element <input type='checkbox' checked> detected with consent wording: 'I agree to communications'
findings.why_it_matters: Under Section 6(1), consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, and an unambiguous indication through clear affirmative action. Pre-ticked boxes are deemed invalid consent under Indian DPDP regulatory interpretations.
findings.recommended_action: Ensure all consent checkboxes default to un-ticked, requiring an active affirmative gesture by the Data Principal.
findings.required_evidence: Updated form markup confirming default unselected state.

AROGYA DIAGNOSTICS CLINIC LTD
ITEMISED PRIVACY NOTICE UNDER SECTION 5 OF THE DPDP ACT, 2023

1. INTRODUCTION & SCOPE
This Privacy Notice is provided by Arogya Diagnostics Clinic Ltd ("Organisation", "we", "us") in compliance with Section 5 of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ("DPDP Act") and Rule 3 of the DPDP Rules, 2025. It applies to all digital personal data collected through our public website (https://arogyaclinic.in), physical intake desks, consultation counters, and diagnostic portals.

2. PERSONAL DATA WE COLLECT
In delivering our services in Healthcare (Clinics & Diagnostics), we may collect the following categories of personal data:
- Personal Identifiers: Full name, age/date of birth, gender, government ID (where required by healthcare or tax law).
- Contact Coordinates: Mobile phone number, postal residential address, and email address.
- Clinical & Transactional Records: Diagnostic test orders, physician consultation summaries, and medical invoices.

3. SPECIFIC PURPOSES OF PROCESSING
Personal data is processed strictly for specified, lawful purposes:
- Purpose A: Scheduling outpatient consultations and diagnostic appointments.
- Purpose B: Generating clinical diagnostic pathology and radiology reports.
- Purpose C: Issuing statutory tax invoices and processing insurance claims.
We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal data.

4. YOUR STATUTORY RIGHTS AS A DATA PRINCIPAL
Under Sections 11–14 of the DPDP Act, you have the right to:
- Access a summary of your personal data processed by us (Section 11).
- Request correction of inaccurate data or completion of incomplete records (Section 12).
- Request erasure of your data once the specified purpose is fulfilled, unless retention is mandated by law (Section 12).
- Nominate another individual to exercise rights on your behalf in the event of death or incapacity (Section 14).

5. WITHDRAWAL OF CONSENT
You may withdraw your consent at any time under Section 6(4) with the same ease with which consent was provided. Upon withdrawal, we will cease processing unless retention is mandated by the Clinical Establishments Act or Income Tax Act. Contact: grievance@organisation.com.

6. GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL OFFICER (SECTION 8(10))
If you have questions or grievances regarding the processing of your personal data, please contact our designated Grievance Officer:
Designation: Grievance & Compliance Officer
Organisation: Arogya Diagnostics Clinic Ltd
Email: grievance@organisation.com
Website: https://arogyaclinic.in
Address: Compliance Department, Registered Office, India

7. ACCESSIBILITY IN 8TH SCHEDULE LANGUAGES
This notice is available in English and Eighth Schedule languages upon request at our reception desks or website language selector.

ITEMISED PRIVACY NOTICE UNDER SECTION 5 OF THE DPDP ACT, 2023

1. INTRODUCTION & SCOPE
This Privacy Notice is provided by Arogya Diagnostics Clinic Ltd ("Organisation", "we", "us") in compliance with Section 5 of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ("DPDP Act") and Rule 3 of the DPDP Rules, 2025. It applies to all digital personal data collected through our public website (https://arogyaclinic.in), physical intake desks, consultation counters, and diagnostic portals.

2. PERSONAL DATA WE COLLECT
In delivering our services in Healthcare (Clinics & Diagnostics), we may collect the following categories of personal data:
- Personal Identifiers: Full name, age/date of birth, gender, government ID (where required by healthcare or tax law).
- Contact Coordinates: Mobile phone number, postal residential address, and email address.
- Clinical & Transactional Records: Diagnostic test orders, physician consultation summaries, and medical invoices.

3. SPECIFIC PURPOSES OF PROCESSING
Personal data is processed strictly for specified, lawful purposes:
- Purpose A: Scheduling outpatient consultations and diagnostic appointments.
- Purpose B: Generating clinical diagnostic pathology and radiology reports.
- Purpose C: Issuing statutory tax invoices and processing insurance claims.
We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal data.

4. YOUR STATUTORY RIGHTS AS A DATA PRINCIPAL
Under Sections 11–14 of the DPDP Act, you have the right to:
- Access a summary of your personal data processed by us (Section 11).
- Request correction of inaccurate data or completion of incomplete records (Section 12).
- Request erasure of your data once the specified purpose is fulfilled, unless retention is mandated by law (Section 12).
- Nominate another individual to exercise rights on your behalf in the event of death or incapacity (Section 14).

5. WITHDRAWAL OF CONSENT
You may withdraw your consent at any time under Section 6(4) with the same ease with which consent was provided. Upon withdrawal, we will cease processing unless retention is mandated by the Clinical Establishments Act or Income Tax Act. Contact: grievance@organisation.com.

6. GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL OFFICER (SECTION 8(10))
If you have questions or grievances regarding the processing of your personal data, please contact our designated Grievance Officer:
Designation: Grievance & Compliance Officer
Organisation: Arogya Diagnostics Clinic Ltd
Email: grievance@organisation.com
Website: https://arogyaclinic.in
Address: Compliance Department, Registered Office, India

7. ACCESSIBILITY IN 8TH SCHEDULE LANGUAGES
This notice is available in English and Eighth Schedule languages upon request at our reception desks or website language selector.

AROGYA DIAGNOSTICS CLINIC LTD
ITEMISED PRIVACY NOTICE UNDER SECTION 5 OF THE DPDP ACT, 2023

1. INTRODUCTION & SCOPE
This Privacy Notice is provided by Arogya Diagnostics Clinic Ltd ("Organisation", "we", "us") in compliance with Section 5 of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ("DPDP Act") and Rule 3 of the DPDP Rules, 2025. It applies to all digital personal data collected through our public website (https://arogyaclinic.in), physical intake desks, consultation counters, and diagnostic portals.

2. PERSONAL DATA WE COLLECT
In delivering our services in Healthcare (Clinics & Diagnostics), we may collect the following categories of personal data:
- Personal Identifiers: Full name, age/date of birth, gender, government ID (where required by healthcare or tax law).
- Contact Coordinates: Mobile phone number, postal residential address, and email address.
- Clinical & Transactional Records: Diagnostic test orders, physician consultation summaries, and medical invoices.

3. SPECIFIC PURPOSES OF PROCESSING
Personal data is processed strictly for specified, lawful purposes:
- Purpose A: Scheduling outpatient consultations and diagnostic appointments.
- Purpose B: Generating clinical diagnostic pathology and radiology reports.
- Purpose C: Issuing statutory tax invoices and processing insurance claims.
We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal data.

4. YOUR STATUTORY RIGHTS AS A DATA PRINCIPAL
Under Sections 11–14 of the DPDP Act, you have the right to:
- Access a summary of your personal data processed by us (Section 11).
- Request correction of inaccurate data or completion of incomplete records (Section 12).
- Request erasure of your data once the specified purpose is fulfilled, unless retention is mandated by law (Section 12).
- Nominate another individual to exercise rights on your behalf in the event of death or incapacity (Section 14).

5. WITHDRAWAL OF CONSENT
You may withdraw your consent at any time under Section 6(4) with the same ease with which consent was provided. Upon withdrawal, we will cease processing unless retention is mandated by the Clinical Establishments Act or Income Tax Act. Contact: grievance@organisation.com.

6. GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL OFFICER (SECTION 8(10))
If you have questions or grievances regarding the processing of your personal data, please contact our designated Grievance Officer:
Designation: Grievance & Compliance Officer
Organisation: Arogya Diagnostics Clinic Ltd
Email: grievance@organisation.com
Website: https://arogyaclinic.in
Address: Compliance Department, Registered Office, India

7. ACCESSIBILITY IN 8TH SCHEDULE LANGUAGES
This notice is available in English and Eighth Schedule languages upon request at our reception desks or website language selector.

DATA BREACH RESPONSE & DUAL-STAGE BOARD INTIMATION SOP (SECTION 8(6))

1. OBJECTIVE
To govern the rapid detection, containment, assessment, and statutory notification of personal data breaches conforming to Section 8(6) of the DPDP Act, 2023 and Rule 7 of the DPDP Rules, 2025.

2. DUAL-STAGE BOARD NOTIFICATION WORKFLOW
Stage 1 (Initial Intimation - Immediate / Without Delay):
- Submit Form A Initial Intimation to the Data Protection Board of India via its digital portal.
- State: nature of incident, date/time discovered, affected data categories, immediate containment actions.

Stage 2 (Supplementary Intimation - Within 72 Hours):
- Submit Form B Comprehensive Intimation within 72 hours.
- Detail: root-cause forensic findings, exact number of affected Data Principals, remediation steps, and individual notice copies.

3. INDIVIDUAL DATA PRINCIPAL NOTIFICATION
Concurrently notify affected Data Principals in clear plain language with recommended safety precautions (e.g., password reset, biometric lock).
